content.value_statement: Notification integrations can fail through incorrect routing, exposed credentials, or incomplete response checks. This skill guides WxPusher integration with protected configuration, explicit failure handling, and mocked tests.
actual_capabilities: Guide standard JSON POST notifications using appToken with UID or Topic recipients.
Guide SPT JSON POST requests while preserving message text and existing token configuration.
Define timeouts, bounded retries, duplicate handling, and top-level plus per-target business-result checks.
Plan protected configuration for local development, containers, CI/CD, and production environments.
Diagnose API failures and WeChat ClawBot binding, activation, and receiving-channel limits.
Specify mocked HTTP tests for request construction, missing configuration, failures, content limits, and credential redaction.
limitations: Provides instructions and reference documentation, not a bundled executable client or hosted notification service.
Requires WxPusher credentials and configured recipients for real notifications; development tests default to mocks.
Cannot guarantee delivery or reading, send to arbitrary WeChat friends or groups, or bypass channel limits.
References can become outdated, and public SPT reset or revocation procedures remain unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Understand WxPusher options
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain UID, Topic, and SPT notifications in WxPusher. Compare their configuration needs and WeChat receiving limits. Do not send messages.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a personal script
prompt_templates.prompt: Add WxPusher failure notifications to my Python task using its existing SPT environment variable. Use JSON POST, bounded retries, and mocked tests only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a small notification workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose missing notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate WxPusher requests that return HTTP 200 without visible notifications. Check redacted business results, recipient configuration, and ClawBot activation. Do not send test messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: diagnose API and receiving-channel failures.

prompt_templates.title: Build a resilient adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate WxPusher behind our notification gateway. Reuse project configuration, isolate failures, validate per-target results, and test retries, deduplication, limits, and redaction with mocks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: integrate reliable notifications into an existing backend.

output_examples.input: Add failure notifications to a Python task using my existing SPT configuration, without sending real messages.
output: Proposed integration: use the existing SPT environment variable and the JSON POST simple-push endpoint.
Failure policy: isolate notification errors and apply bounded retries only to transient failures.
Validation plan: mock successful responses, business failures, missing configuration, and timeouts.
Live-send status: no real message is required for this development workflow.

output_examples.input: WxPusher returns HTTP 200, but WeChat shows no notification. What should I check?
output: Check the top-level and per-target business codes before treating the request as accepted.
If accepted, check the intended recipient and ClawBot binding, enablement, activation, and channel allowance.
Do not use discontinued status-query responses as a reason to resend.
An accepted request does not confirm that the user received or read the notification.

best_practices: Reuse project secret storage and HTTP clients; keep credentials, recipient data, and sensitive content out of logs.
Default to mocked tests and perform real sends only within explicit authorization for purpose, recipients, and frequency.
Validate business results and content limits; use bounded retries and deduplication where repeated notifications would cause harm.
anti_patterns: Treating HTTP 200 or a created sending task as proof that a user received or read a notification.
Committing tokens, logging authenticated URLs, or copying full request bodies into notification messages.
Retrying authentication failures indefinitely, bypassing channel limits, or changing recipients without authorization.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when WxPusher is explicitly requested or already selected. A generic request for WeChat notifications does not select WxPusher automatically.

faq.question: Does this skill include a ready-made client?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions and reference documentation for integration through your project's existing tools and libraries.

faq.question: Can development proceed without real credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Use named environment variables, placeholders, and mocked HTTP responses. Real notifications require configured credentials, recipients, and authorization.

faq.question: Can it send to any WeChat friend or group?
faq.answer: No. The references describe notifications to configured recipients through supported channels. WeChat ClawBot requires binding and activation and has channel limits.

faq.question: How does SPT differ from standard notifications?
faq.answer: SPT uses a separate push token instead of appToken with UID or Topic routing. The skill defaults to JSON POST for SPT.

faq.question: Can a leaked SPT be reset like an appToken?
faq.answer: The references do not verify a public SPT reset or revocation method. Stop spreading the token and contact WxPusher for confirmed recovery options.
